name: Sotorasib
originator: Amgen (building on Kevan Shokat's switch-II pocket discovery at UCSF)

discovery.note: Exploits a cryptic pocket next to the mutant cysteine 12 in GDP-bound KRAS G12C, first described by Shokat's laboratory in 2013.

tagline: First approved KRAS inhibitor, targeting a mutation once thought 'undruggable'
summary: Sotorasib is a covalent inhibitor that locks the KRAS G12C mutant protein in its inactive GDP-bound state. It was the first drug approved to target KRAS, a long-elusive oncogene, and is used for KRAS G12C-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer and, with panitumumab, colorectal cancer.
mechanism: The G12C mutation introduces a cysteine that sits next to the 'switch-II pocket' of KRAS. Sotorasib binds this pocket and forms an irreversible bond with cysteine 12, but only when KRAS is in the inactive GDP-bound state.

Trapping KRAS G12C in this state prevents nucleotide exchange to active GTP-KRAS and shuts down RAF–MEK–ERK signalling. In colorectal cancer, feedback reactivation of EGFR signalling limits single-agent activity, which is why it is combined with the anti-EGFR antibody panitumumab.
uses: KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after at least one prior systemic therapy
KRAS G12C-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer, with panitumumab, after chemotherapy

history.title: Switch-II pocket
history.detail: Ostrem, Shokat and colleagues (Nature) describe covalent inhibitors of KRAS G12C binding an allosteric pocket.

history.title: First-in-human data
history.detail: Amgen reports AMG 510 clinical activity and publishes its structure (Nature).

history.title: Accelerated approval
history.detail: FDA approves Lumakras for KRAS G12C NSCLC based on CodeBreaK 100.

history.title: CodeBreaK 200 and FDA letter
history.detail: Phase 3 shows improved progression-free but not overall survival versus docetaxel; FDA declines conversion to full approval and requests another confirmatory study.

history.title: Colorectal cancer
history.detail: FDA approves sotorasib with panitumumab for KRAS G12C-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer (CodeBreaK 300).

serious: hepatotoxicity, especially soon after checkpoint inhibitors

facts: KRAS G12C is found in roughly 13% of lung adenocarcinomas and 3–4% of colorectal cancers.
